purpose: Visual design reference for P15. Generated incidental score/grid labels, copy, values and geometry do not define behavior or change the existing workstation.

image.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one polished high-fidelity screenshot as the visual reference for a real new Backing waveform view inside TabPlayer, a cross-platform Rust/Tauri music notation and tablature editor. Match a compact professional music workstation, not a marketing concept. This is a flat practical desktop application, screen 1600x1000. Charcoal #171a20 backdrop and #23272f panels, fine #434b59 dividers, readable #edf0f5 text and #b5bfcc labels, restrained #79aaff blue selected/focus states, small 3px corners, system sans 12–14px equivalent. Warm cream #fffdf2 notation paper, black sheet music. Subdued violet waveform is functional audio data, not decorative wallpaper. No glow, glass, gradients, soft cards or product logos.
Layout follows the existing TabPlayer shell. Top compact menu row reads TabPlayer, File, View, Undo, Redo, Help. Below two document tabs: Harbour study.tabplayer active and Bass sketch. Transport row Play, Stop, 0:08 / 0:32, Speed 100%, Metronome, 120 BPM. Narrow left pane 208px with Track, Sound, Backing tabs; Backing selected. Left pane title Backing audio, filename Harbour rhythm.wav, duration 32.0 s. Small Import/Replace and Remove controls; Backing offset (ms) 0; Gain slider; Pan slider; Mute and Solo checkboxes; disclosure Synchronization anchors and two modest numeric anchor rows, no extra effects. Central upper area is cream music notation with guitar staff and six-string TAB, title Harbour study, a few bars labeled1–8, bar5 lightly selected blue. Right Inspector 304px, restrained existing Edit/Practice/Presentation tabs and simple beat information. No modal dialog.
The NEW view is in the existing bottom dock spanning the full left-plus-center workspace, ending at the inspector. Give the dock approximately280px height so it is readable. Dock tabs read Overview, Mixer, Instrument, Backing; Backing selected in blue, Hide at far right. Within the Backing view: one compact toolbar 'Harbour rhythm.wav' then Zoom out button, '100%' label, Zoom in button, Fit button. Below the toolbar a clearly labeled seconds ruler 0:00 0:04 0:08 0:12 0:16 0:20 0:24 0:28 0:32. Under it a REALISTIC single continuous audio waveform on a near-black plot, using restrained violet vertical sample peaks with silence and attack structure. Fine vertical grid lines carry score labels 'M1 · 1', 'M2 · 1', 'M3 · 1', 'M4 · 1', 'M5 · 1', etc, representing measure and performed occurrence; subtle beat divisions. Two small blue triangular sync handles sit on this waveform at audio0:00 and0:08, with a fine solid vertical line down to the plot. The second handle is selected with a visible blue focus outline. A separate thin cream or white cursor marks the matched selected score/audio position. Clearly distinct handles and cursor, no arbitrary many-colored lanes, fake meters or automation curves. One small horizontal scrollbar below the plot. Dock footer readout is easy to scan: 'Selected sync point · Measure5 · Occurrence1 · Position0.00 · Audio8,000ms'. Beside it real controls 'Add sync point' and 'Delete sync point'. Make exact relationships legible, not tiny captions. Keep every control aligned on a disciplined desktop grid, useful spacing and visible focus.
This image is a design reference only; audio shape and score are illustrative. Do not add AI labels, tutorials, pitch shift, tempo extraction, spectral tools, trim/loop waveform editing, file browsing dialogs, tempo-generation buttons, download icons, marketing copy, sidecar cards or invented app features. Output only the app screenshot.
image.review: Root inspected the actual generated image. Adopt charcoal/cream/blue shell, compact toolbar, violet waveform, seconds ruler, score grid and distinct focused sync handles. Existing dock continues to end before Inspector; its default height remains current adaptive geometry. Correct score/bar/audio relationships derive from runtime tempo/occurrence/map, not illustrative labels. Preserve existing numeric anchor controls, not generated simplified rows. No changed Gain dB units or toolbar/inspector redesign.
